name: Sojourner and Pathfinder
summary: The first rover to drive on Mars, planned for about a week and active for 83 sols.
discoveries: Proved that a small rover could drive and study rocks on Mars.
Operated for 83 sols after a planned mission of 7, about twelve times its design life.

stories.kids: I was a tiny rover, and I was the first to ever drive on Mars. I was only supposed to work for about a week. I kept going for 83 Martian days and showed the world that rovers on Mars were possible.
stories.explorer: Sojourner rode to Mars on the Pathfinder lander in July 1997. It was designed for 7 sols, but it kept working for 83. Pathfinder’s last successful transmission was in late September 1997.
stories.scientist: Mars Pathfinder landed at Ares Vallis on July 4, 1997. The Sojourner rover was designed for 7 sols and operated for 83 sols. The final data transmission from Pathfinder was received on September 27, 1997.

image.alt: The Sojourner rover on the rocky surface of Mars, with its solar panel on top and six wheels on the ground.

clues.explain: I worked for 83 sols, about twelve times my design life.

timeline.title: Landing on Mars
timeline.text: Mars Pathfinder lands at Ares Vallis, carrying the Sojourner rover.

timeline.title: Last transmission
timeline.text: Pathfinder’s final data transmission arrives. Sojourner worked for 83 sols, with only 7 planned.

learn.title: Who I am
learn.text: I’m Sojourner, a tiny six-wheeled rover. I rode to Mars on the Mars Pathfinder lander and we landed on July 4, 1997.

learn.title: My mission
learn.text: I was designed to work for 7 sols, about a week. A sol is one Martian day, a little longer than an Earth day.

learn.title: How it went
learn.text: I kept going for 83 sols, about twelve times my design life. Pathfinder’s last data transmission arrived on September 27, 1997.
